blocks.text:
After breakfast, transfer to the airport for your flight to Iguaçu. On arrival, we’ll meet you and take you to your hotel before you set out for the Brazilian side of the falls.

The Iguaçu Falls lie in the canyon of the Iguaçu River, in a national park rich in plant and animal life. The falls are thought to have formed through volcanic activity and shifts in layers of rock. Their name means “big water” in Guaraní.

The site comprises 275 waterfalls. Water pours into the gorge and rainbows form in the spray. The best-known section is the Devil’s Throat. On the way there, you’ll see smaller cascades and the surrounding rainforest.

blocks.text:
This morning we return to the Brazilian side of Iguaçu Falls. The falls are often called the seventh wonder of the world. The Guaraní name means “big water,” which captures the force of 275 cascades plunging into the gorge.

You can see the falls from both Brazil and Argentina. The Devil’s Throat is one of the most striking spots. Trails and viewing platforms let you see the cascades from different distances and heights.

At the Devil’s Throat, spray rises into the air and rainbows appear above the gorge. You’ll have time to walk the trails and take photographs.
